exam.title: GitHub Certified: Agentic AI Developer
exam.passScore: Microsoft certification exams usually require 700 or greater. Confirm on the official page before sitting the exam.

domains.title: Prepare agent architecture and SDLC processes
domains.summary: Design where agents fit in the SDLC, define boundaries, and make work inspectable before execution.
topics: Map agent responsibilities to SDLC stages
Identify which steps agents should perform
Recognise and mitigate common agent anti-patterns
Define inputs, outputs, success criteria, and done criteria
Separate planning, reasoning, and execution
Require structured plans before action
Validate plans before letting agents act
Prevent unapproved execution
Set autonomy levels and intervention points
Produce inspectable artifacts inside standard development tools
Use pull requests, checks, CODEOWNERS, rulesets, and environment gates as control points
practice: Create a GitHub issue template for an agent task with inputs, outputs, risks, acceptance criteria, and rollback plan.
Write a repository custom instruction that forces plan first, no execution until approval.
Design a PR governance flow for an agent-created feature.

domains.title: Implement tool use and environment interaction
domains.summary: Configure tools, MCP servers, permissions, execution contexts, CI invocation, safe error handling, and traceability.
topics: Identify required tools for an agent task
Configure agent tools and permissions
Use least privilege for tool access
Configure MCP servers as tools
Configure GitHub remote MCP server concepts
Understand MCP registries and allow lists
Evaluate execution context
Scope agents to a repository, branch, environment, or workflow
Invoke agents from CI workflows
Allow autonomous branch and pull request creation safely
Handle environment-specific constraints
Implement retries, rollbacks, escalation paths, and traceability
practice: Create a sample MCP configuration with only read-only tools allowlisted.
Create a CI workflow that runs validation before an agent PR can merge.
Write an error handling policy for failed tool calls.

domains.title: Manage memory, state, and execution
domains.summary: Keep task context useful, current, scoped, and recoverable across long-running agent work.
topics: Choose short-term, long-term, and external memory strategies
Scope memory to task-relevant information
Define memory expiration, pruning, and reset rules
Persist decisions and task progress as durable artifacts
Resume work without repeating steps
Detect and correct context drift
Share agent state without conflict
Prevent stale or conflicting context across tools and environments
practice: Create a DECISIONS.md log template for agent projects.
Write rules for what memory should never contain, including secrets and personal data.

domains.title: Perform evaluation, error analysis, and tuning
domains.summary: Judge agent outputs using measurable signals, artefacts, scans, traces, and root cause analysis.
topics: Define expected outcomes and operational constraints
Identify qualitative and quantitative evaluation signals
Align evaluation with developer intent
Use automated scans as evaluation signals
Inspect logs, plans, traces, outputs, and workflow artifacts
Classify reasoning errors, tool misuse, context errors, and environment errors
Revise instructions, workflows, constraints, memory use, and tool access
Avoid tuning that hides real defects
practice: Create an agent QA scorecard with pass, risk, and fail categories.
Analyse a failed agent PR and classify the root cause.
Rewrite a vague prompt into an evaluable task contract.

domains.title: Orchestrate multi-agent coordination
domains.summary: Coordinate multiple agents without duplicated effort, conflicting changes, hidden handoffs, or unsafe parallel execution.
topics: Apply orchestration patterns
Configure isolation for parallel execution
Detect overlapping code changes and duplicated effort
Resolve contradictory outputs
Produce reviewable artifacts for multi-agent workflows
Document decisions, handoffs, and outcomes
Perform post-hoc analysis of multi-agent behaviour
Identify failed, partial, stalled, or degraded executions
Implement rollback and human-in-the-loop recovery
Add, update, replace, and retire agents while preserving auditability
practice: Design planner, builder, reviewer, and release-gate agents for one feature.
Create a conflict resolution matrix for agent PRs.
Write a retirement checklist for a deprecated agent profile.

domains.title: Implement guardrails and accountability
domains.summary: Classify risk, apply explicit authorisation where needed, enforce least privilege, and preserve speed without pretending risky work is safe.
topics: Classify actions by operational, security, and compliance risk
Assign autonomy levels
Identify actions requiring human judgement
Block actions violating security, compliance, or Responsible AI policy
Scope permissions and execution contexts
Require explicit authorisation for irreversible or sensitive changes
Minimise approvals that do not materially reduce risk
Preserve accountability through logs, PRs, approvals, artifacts, and decision records
practice: Create an autonomy matrix from low-risk read-only work to high-risk production changes.
Write a policy for secrets, credentials, production data, and destructive commands.
Design a human approval checkpoint that does not block harmless automation.
